description: Coaching tips indexed by dimension and score range. Coaches use these to communicate with clients about specific aspects of a recipe, set expectations, and provide actionable guidance.

1_to_2.label: Quick Meal
1_to_2.coaching_message: This recipe can be made in under 15 minutes. Perfect for busy days when you need food fast.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: This will be on the table before delivery would arrive. Fast, fresh, and satisfying.
preparation_tips: Even quick recipes benefit from having ingredients out before starting
Keep a few of these recipes memorized for no-plan nights

3_to_4.label: Weeknight Ready
3_to_4.coaching_message: A 20-40 minute recipe that fits into most weeknight schedules. Manageable even on busy days.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: This is a solid weeknight option. With a little prep, you can have a great meal on a normal evening.
preparation_tips: Chop vegetables during a spare 5 minutes earlier in the day if possible
Start the longest-cooking component first (usually the grain or starch)
Clean as you go to reduce post-dinner cleanup

5_to_6.label: Planned Meal
5_to_6.coaching_message: This recipe requires 45-75 minutes. Plan for it on an evening when you have some breathing room.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: Carving out an hour for cooking can be meditative. Put on music or a podcast and enjoy the process.
preparation_tips: Prep the night before: chop vegetables, marinate proteins, measure dry ingredients
Use passive cooking time (simmering, baking) to clean up or prep other components
Double the recipe if it freezes well to get two meals for the time of one

7_to_8.label: Weekend Project
7_to_8.coaching_message: Plan 1.5-3 hours for this recipe. Best saved for weekends or days when you can enjoy the process.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: Think of this as an activity, not a chore. Cooking at this pace allows flavors to develop that quick meals cannot achieve.
preparation_tips: Make it a cooking event: invite a friend or partner to help
Break it into phases: prep in the morning, cook in the afternoon
If there is a long passive time (marinating, proofing), use that time for something else
Consider making extra for the freezer

9_to_10.label: All-Day Affair
9_to_10.coaching_message: This recipe is a significant time investment, potentially spanning several hours or requiring advance preparation. Treat it as a special project.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: This is cooking as craft. Set aside the time, commit to the process, and the results will be worth it.
preparation_tips: Read the full recipe the day before and create a shopping list
Identify any overnight steps (marinating, proofing, chilling) and plan around them
Start early in the day so you are not racing against dinner time
Play music, pour yourself a beverage, and treat it as an experience

nutrition.note: Nutrition mesh-axis score uses an inverse scale: 1 = healthiest, 10 = least healthy. Raw per-serving values (calories, macros, glycemic_index) live in nutrition.json.

1_to_2.label: Excellent Choice
1_to_2.coaching_message: This is an outstanding nutritional choice. High in beneficial nutrients and low in concerning elements.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: This meal aligns perfectly with your health goals. Enjoy it knowing your body is getting what it needs.
1_to_2.nutrition_highlights: Rich in nutrients, balanced macros, minimal sodium and added sugar
1_to_2.dietary_notes: Suitable for nearly any dietary goal. Modify portion size to match caloric targets.

3_to_4.label: Good Choice
3_to_4.coaching_message: A solidly nutritious option. May have one minor nutritional trade-off but overall healthy.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: This is a smart choice. Not perfect, but close. The satisfaction you get will support consistent healthy eating.
3_to_4.nutrition_highlights: Good nutrient density with one area that could be improved
3_to_4.dietary_notes: Consider the trade-off (e.g., higher sodium but excellent protein). Adjust the rest of the day to compensate.

5_to_6.label: Moderate Choice
5_to_6.coaching_message: This recipe has nutritional strengths and weaknesses in roughly equal measure. Fine in moderation.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: Not every meal needs to be perfect. This can fit in a balanced week if you make smarter choices at other meals.
5_to_6.nutrition_highlights: Mixed nutritional profile: some benefits offset by some concerns
5_to_6.dietary_notes: Consider modifications: reduce oil, use leaner protein, add more vegetables, or reduce the portion slightly.
healthier_swaps: Add an extra serving of vegetables
Substitute whole grain for refined grain
Reduce sodium by half and add acid (lemon, vinegar)

7_to_8.label: Occasional Choice
7_to_8.coaching_message: This recipe leans toward indulgent. Save it for special occasions and balance it with lighter meals the same day.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: It is okay to enjoy indulgent food occasionally. The key is not making it a habit.
7_to_8.nutrition_highlights: Higher in calories, sodium, sugar, or unhealthy fats than ideal
7_to_8.dietary_notes: Limit to once per week maximum. Pair with a large salad or vegetable side. Consider a smaller portion.
healthier_swaps: Use half the butter or oil called for
Substitute Greek yogurt for sour cream or cream
Add vegetables to every plate to reduce the proportion of the indulgent component

9_to_10.label: Rare Indulgence
9_to_10.coaching_message: This recipe is nutritionally dense in the wrong direction. Reserve for rare special occasions.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: Life includes celebrations. Enjoy it fully when you choose it, then return to your plan at the next meal.
9_to_10.nutrition_highlights: Very high in calories, saturated fat, sodium, or sugar
9_to_10.dietary_notes: Make this the exception, not the rule. Balance the rest of the day with lighter, vegetable-forward meals.
healthier_swaps: Reduce the portion to half and add a large side salad
Make it as directed but only serve yourself a small portion
Look for a lighter version of the same dish and try it next time
Skip alcohol or dessert on the same day

1_to_2.label: Minimal Steps
1_to_2.coaching_message: Very few steps. You can practically make this from memory after one or two attempts.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: This is barely cooking... in the best way. Simple, fast, and satisfying.
preparation_tips: Memorize these recipes for no-plan nights
Consider doubling for leftovers

3_to_4.label: Straightforward Process
3_to_4.coaching_message: A reasonable number of steps that flow logically. Easy to follow without getting lost.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: Each step builds naturally on the last. You will not feel overwhelmed.
preparation_tips: Group your steps mentally: prep phase and cook phase
Do not skip steps but do not overthink them either

5_to_6.label: Multiple Steps
5_to_6.coaching_message: Several steps requiring attention to sequence. Read through first and plan your flow.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: This recipe has a rhythm. Once you find it, it flows naturally. Trust the process.
preparation_tips: Read all steps before starting
Note which steps can happen simultaneously
Mark the recipe with timing notes: which step takes the longest?
Clean between steps when there is a natural pause

7_to_8.label: Many Steps
7_to_8.coaching_message: A significant number of steps, some of which may overlap. Good preparation is essential.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: This is where mise en place matters. Pre-measure everything, line up your ingredients, and you will navigate the steps smoothly.
preparation_tips: Complete all prep before starting any cooking
Write out a simplified checklist of steps in order
Identify which steps have passive wait time you can use for other steps
Have all equipment clean and ready before you start

9_to_10.label: Complex Sequence
9_to_10.coaching_message: A demanding number of steps, likely with overlapping processes and critical timing. Approach this as a project.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: Professional chefs practice complex recipes multiple times. Your first attempt is a learning experience. The result gets better each time.
preparation_tips: Rewrite the recipe as a personal checklist with your own notes
Practice any unfamiliar techniques separately before starting the full recipe
Set multiple timers for key moments
Have a friend or partner assist with transitions between steps
Plan cleanup breaks during passive cooking times

1_to_2.label: Minimal Cleanup
1_to_2.coaching_message: Almost no cleanup required. A quick wash and you are done.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: One-pan wonder! Dinner and cleanup done in under 10 minutes total.
tips: When cleanup is this easy, double the batch and freeze half

3_to_4.label: Standard Cleanup
3_to_4.coaching_message: Normal amount of dishes. 10-15 minutes of cleanup after dinner.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: Standard dinner, standard cleanup. Nothing daunting here.
tips: Clean as you go during passive cooking steps
Soak anything with stuck-on food while you eat

5_to_6.label: Notable Cleanup
5_to_6.coaching_message: Significant cleanup involved. Plan for 20-30 minutes of washing after eating.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: The meal is worth the cleanup. Make it a team effort: one person washes, one dries and puts away.
tips: Fill the sink with soapy water before you start cooking
Use parchment paper or foil to line baking sheets
Rinse pots and pans immediately after use to prevent sticking
Consider making this recipe on a day when you have energy for both cooking and cleaning

7_to_8.label: Heavy Cleanup
7_to_8.coaching_message: This recipe uses many pots, pans, and tools. Cleanup will be substantial.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: Consider this a special-occasion recipe. The experience is worth the aftermath.
tips: Run the dishwasher before you start so it is empty and ready
Designate a cleanup person if cooking for others
Line every surface you can with foil or parchment
Use one cutting board for everything in order, washing between uses if needed
Plan for leftovers so you get multiple meals from one cleanup session

9_to_10.label: Major Cleanup Event
9_to_10.coaching_message: This recipe will leave your kitchen in need of serious attention. Plan accordingly.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: Some meals are memorable enough to justify the mess. Plan a recovery strategy.
tips: Accept that cleanup is part of the experience and budget time for it
Use disposable liners wherever possible
Clean in stages during the cooking process (during passive times)
If you have help, assign one person to start cleanup before the meal is served
Make enough for leftovers to amortize the cleanup cost over multiple meals

ingredients.note: Score reflects the count of distinct ingredients only (1-2 = roughly 1-5 items, 9-10 = 26+ items)

1_to_2.label: Few Ingredients
1_to_2.coaching_message: A short ingredient list of just a handful of items. Quick to shop for and easy to keep track of while cooking.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: Barely a shopping list. Grab a few things and you are ready to go.
tips: Great for no-plan nights when you do not want a big shop
Keep these staples stocked so you can make it on a whim

3_to_4.label: Short List
3_to_4.coaching_message: A modest number of ingredients. Manageable for a single grocery run and easy to lay out before you start.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: Nothing overwhelming here. One trip to the store covers it.
tips: Check your pantry first to avoid buying duplicates
Lay everything out before cooking so nothing gets missed

5_to_6.label: Moderate List
5_to_6.coaching_message: A fuller ingredient list. Worth organizing your mise en place so you do not lose track mid-recipe.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: More to gather, but a little organization keeps it smooth.
tips: Group ingredients by recipe stage as you prep
Measure everything out before turning on any heat

7_to_8.label: Long List
7_to_8.coaching_message: A lot of distinct ingredients. Budget extra shopping and prep time, and double-check nothing is forgotten.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: It is a bigger gather, but ticking items off a list keeps it under control.
tips: Shop from a written checklist and tick items off
Pre-portion ingredients into bowls so the cook itself flows quickly

9_to_10.label: Very Long List
9_to_10.coaching_message: An extensive ingredient list. This is a project recipe to shop for carefully and prep well in advance.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: Long lists look daunting, but full mise en place turns it into assembly.
tips: Do a complete shop the day before and verify every item
Set out every pre-measured ingredient before you begin cooking
Consider whether any ingredients can be prepped a day ahead

reproducibility.note: Higher reproducibility scores (7-10) mean harder to reproduce consistently

1_to_2.label: Highly Reproducible
1_to_2.coaching_message: This recipe is very forgiving and produces consistent results every time. Great for building confidence.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: You can make this on autopilot. It will turn out well even if your technique is not perfect.
tips: Memorize this recipe as a reliable go-to
Good candidate for meal prep since it will be consistent across batches

3_to_4.label: Mostly Reproducible
3_to_4.coaching_message: Generally consistent with minor variations. Most home cooks can get good results reliably.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: This recipe will work well for you. Small variations in outcome are normal and part of home cooking.
tips: Follow measurements closely the first time, then adjust to taste on future attempts
Take notes on what worked and what you would change

5_to_6.label: Moderate Reproducibility
5_to_6.coaching_message: Results may vary based on technique, ingredients, and conditions. Pay attention to details.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: Each attempt teaches you something. Your second time will be better than your first.
tips: Follow the recipe exactly the first time before making modifications
Note any environmental factors (humidity, altitude) that may affect results
Use measured ingredients rather than volume when precision matters
Accept that some variation is normal and not a failure

7_to_8.label: Variable Results
7_to_8.coaching_message: This recipe's results depend heavily on technique and conditions. Expect variability between attempts.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: This is a recipe that rewards practice. Your results will improve with each attempt.
tips: Keep detailed notes on each attempt
Invest in a kitchen scale for precise measurements
Control environmental factors when possible (oven thermometer, room temperature)
Practice the key technique separately before attempting the full recipe

9_to_10.label: Requires Mastery
9_to_10.coaching_message: This recipe demands precise technique and conditions for consistent results. It may take many attempts.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: Even professional chefs practice challenging techniques for years. Each attempt brings you closer to mastery.
tips: Watch videos of each technique before attempting
Consider taking a class or seeking one-on-one coaching for key techniques
Accept that your first 2-3 attempts may not produce the desired result
Keep a detailed journal of each attempt with photos
Focus on mastering one technique at a time rather than the entire recipe

cost.note: Score reflects estimated cost per serving (1-2 = budget, 9-10 = splurge). Author provides a total for the recipe's stated servings; the serving calculator scales it.

1_to_2.label: Budget Friendly
1_to_2.coaching_message: Very low cost per serving. An easy choice when stretching a grocery budget.
1_to_2.client_encouragement: Cheap, cheerful, and easy on the wallet. Perfect for regular rotation.
tips: Great backbone for a weekly meal plan
Batch-cook to drive the per-serving cost even lower

3_to_4.label: Everyday Cost
3_to_4.coaching_message: A typical weeknight price per serving. Reasonable for regular cooking.
3_to_4.client_encouragement: Solid value for a normal meal. Nothing that will dent the budget.
tips: Buy core ingredients in larger sizes when they keep well
Watch for sales on the main protein to bring the cost down

5_to_6.label: Moderate Spend
5_to_6.coaching_message: A step up in cost per serving. Fine in the rotation, but not the cheapest option.
5_to_6.client_encouragement: Worth it now and then. Balance it with budget-friendly meals across the week.
tips: Pair pricier mains with inexpensive sides to balance the plate cost
Scale servings up so leftovers spread the cost across more meals

7_to_8.label: Premium
7_to_8.coaching_message: A higher cost per serving. Best treated as a planned treat rather than an everyday meal.
7_to_8.client_encouragement: A treat-yourself meal. Plan for it and savor it.
tips: Reserve for occasions where the splurge is the point
Check whether a cheaper cut or ingredient swap keeps most of the appeal

9_to_10.label: Splurge
9_to_10.coaching_message: A very high cost per serving. A special-occasion recipe to budget for deliberately.
9_to_10.client_encouragement: This is a celebration meal. When the occasion calls for it, it is worth every dollar.
tips: Save for milestones and celebrations
Make exactly the servings you need to avoid costly waste
